lessons: Redo the full ticket from the merge base. Review found the incremental read and the pure no-I/O helper sound: it parses complete lines from an offset, returns the new offset and line count, and leaves an unterminated tail unparsed. Rebuild them the same way.

append() must never go through read_segments() or touch rolled segments. Per the Scope in, it refreshes only the active segment through the instance's incremental read, parses only lines it has not cached, and takes the roll-age timestamp from that segment's first line.

Put the active-segment incremental update in one place that both read_segments() and append() call, taking one segment path. A fresh instance's first append() then parses the active segment once, and a corrupt rolled segment never blocks a write.

Add a test that a fresh Journal's first append() over a rolled segment plus an active segment makes no _parse_line calls for rolled-segment lines. This pins the Scope in rule that append parses only the active segment.

Criterion 2, same-instance case: keep the read() result after the k appends and assert it equals Journal(tmp_path, clock).read() by value and order, as the second-writer case does. Do not compare only body['n'].
